speaker: Doctor
text: I need to understand what happened during your loss of consciousness. Did you lose muscle tone and collapse, or did you stiffen up and thrash around? This distinction is critical for my next steps.

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the timing right after urination is very specific. Does this episode occur more frequently, such as every time you urinate, or was it an isolated event? Also, have you experienced any chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath leading up to the loss of consciousness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episode of loss of consciousness. I also have Regained consciousness quickly without confusion, No urinary incontinence, No bite marks or injuries.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The rapid recovery without confusion strongly suggests a vasovagal mechanism, often triggered by the Valsalva maneuver during urination. Have you noticed any dizziness, nausea, or sweating immediately before you passed out? Additionally, do you have a history of heart disease or high blood pressure?
